after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 3=6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=1\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 2=4.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,4\,|\cdot 6 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
The triangle $D$ has vertices $(2,2),(5,2),(4,5).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}
content.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069841/assets/aef99dd5276166e5c7b4fb2f716b060390b6577f2d3625dd5dc835bcec6c4856.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 3=\frac{9}{2}.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=(-5)\cdot (-2)-0\cdot 0=10.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,10\,|\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =45.\end{aligned}
$$
